std:negate.label: Negate
std:negate.description: Arithmetic negation. Number → Number. Counterpart to the unary `-` operator (Prefixable).

std:clamp.label: Clamp
std:clamp.description: Constrain a number between min and max

std:lerp.label: Linear interpolate
std:lerp.description: Linear interpolation: lerp a b t = a + (b - a) * t. At t=0 returns a, at t=1 returns b. Not clamped — t outside [0, 1] extrapolates.

std:isMultipleOf.label: Is multiple of
std:isMultipleOf.description: True when `value` is an integer multiple of `num/den` (within IEEE-754 tolerance 1e-9). Used by field-editor's number-resolution refinement: `isMultipleOf value 1 100` accepts hundredths (cents).

std:isUuid.label: Is UUID
std:isUuid.description: True for the canonical text form of an RFC 4122 UUID: 36 characters, hyphens at positions 8, 13, 18 and 23, hexadecimal digits elsewhere in either case, version 1-5 and the RFC variant.

std:isUuidDigits.label: UUID digits and hyphens
std:isUuidDigits.description: For a 36-character text: hyphens at positions 8, 13, 18 and 23 and hexadecimal digits (either case) everywhere else. Part of isUuid.

std:isUuidVersion.label: UUID version and variant
std:isUuidVersion.description: For a 36-character text: version digit 1-5 and the RFC variant (8, 9, a or b). Part of isUuid.

std:id.label: Identity
std:id.description: Return the argument unchanged. ∀a. a → a

std:const.label: Const
std:const.description: Ignore the second argument and return the first. ∀a b. a → b → a

std:count.label: Count
std:count.description: Number of elements in a list. ∀a. List a → ℕ

std:appendItem.label: Append item
std:appendItem.description: Append a single element to the end of a list. ∀a. a → List a → List a. Equivalent to `arr ++ [item]` in Haskell — the natural 1-element snoc that pairs with `concat` for chained appends. Phase 21.2 introduced this as the primitive that plays the role of TS's `arr.push(item)` in accumulator-threaded Fenel bodies (bare-array literals like `[item]` are rejected by Core IR at expression position, so a dedicated primitive is the self-hosting path).

std:fromMaybe.label: From Maybe
std:fromMaybe.description: Unwrap a Maybe to its value, or the supplied default when Nothing. ∀a. a → Maybe a → a (Haskell `fromMaybe`, default-first). The canonical Maybe eliminator — fromMaybe {} m, fromMaybe "" m, fromMaybe [] (tail xs) subsume the ad-hoc default-on-absence helpers.

std:escapeHtml.label: Escape HTML
std:escapeHtml.description: Substitute the 5-character HTML-attribute-safe escape set (&, ", ', <, >) in a string. Composes std:replaceAll. Used by the redirect route's HTML template; future HTML-rendering surfaces consume the same primitive.

std:imageRetro.label: Retro
std:imageRetro.description: grayscale → pixelate. A composition (no native) — the storybook shows both intermediate stages.

std:validateDateResolution.label: Validate date resolution
std:validateDateResolution.description: True when `value`'s ISO precision fits within `level` (year / month / day / hour / minute / second). Used by field-editor's date-resolution refinement.

std:geoLevelDepth.label: Geo level depth
std:geoLevelDepth.description: Depth index (0–5) of a GeoLevel constructor in the canonical Country → Address ordering. Phase 4 of field-meta-collapse — underpins the `Resolvable` typeclass instances for `Place : GeoLevel -> Type`.

std:compareGeoLevel.label: Compare geo level
std:compareGeoLevel.description: Compare two GeoLevel constructors by depth — returns -1 if `a` is coarser, 0 if equal, 1 if `a` is finer. Phase 4 of field-meta-collapse — supersedes treeLattice's `compare` method for geography. Used by the `Resolvable` typeclass instances dispatched off the phantom level.

std:regionalIndicator.label: Regional indicator letter
std:regionalIndicator.description: Map an uppercase ASCII letter A..Z to its Regional Indicator Symbol emoji 🇦..🇿. Helper for std:countryFlag (storage-as-effect Phase 3c).

std:countryFlag.label: Country flag
std:countryFlag.description: Derive a country's flag emoji from its ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (US → 🇺🇸). Pure projection: the two Regional Indicator Symbol letters for the code, concatenated. The source of truth for a country's flag — replaces the baked `_flag` field on the country reference rows (storage-as-effect Phase 3c, D5 slice 3).

std:and.label: And
std:and.description: Logical AND — true when both operands are truthy. Short-circuit via if-lowering (Phase 5b6): `b` is only evaluated when `a` is true.

std:or.label: Or
std:or.description: Logical OR — true when either operand is truthy. Short-circuit via if-lowering (Phase 5b6): `b` is only evaluated when `a` is false.

std:not.label: Not
std:not.description: Logical negation — body is `if x then False else True` via if-lowering (Phase 5b7).

std:ifElse.label: If-else
std:ifElse.description: Choose between two already evaluated values. ∀a. Boolean → a → a → a. Function arguments are eager; use the structural if form when only the selected branch expression should evaluate.

std:tryParseBoolean.label: Try parse boolean
std:tryParseBoolean.description: Attempt to parse a string as a Boolean. Recognises yes/y/true/1/ok/yep/yeah → Just true and no/n/false/0/nope/nah → Just false (case-insensitive, trimmed). Returns Nothing for anything else. Conformant Maybe(Boolean) return shape (Phase 5b9 — pre-5b9 the TS native returned non-conformant `null` for the unknown case; callers using legacy `match [_, null, ...]` patterns must update to `match [_, {$tag: "Nothing"}, ...]`).

std:bindResult.label: Bind Result (>>=)
std:bindResult.description: Result-monad bind / Kleisli arrow chaining. `bindResult r f` returns Err e unchanged when r is Err, otherwise applies f to the Ok value. Lets composite computations short-circuit at the first failure without nesting case-of at each step. ∀e a b. Result e a → (a → Result e b) → Result e b.

std:..label: Compose (.)
std:..description: Function composition operator: (f . g)(x) = f(g(x)). Infix alias for `compose`. ∀a b c. (b → c) → (a → b) → (a → c)

std:$.label: Apply ($)
std:$.description: Function application as a low-precedence right-assoc operator. f $ x = f x. ∀a b. (a → b) → a → b

std:recordType.label: Record type
std:recordType.description: Build a `$record` FenelType value from a list of field-entry records: [FieldEntry] → {$record: {fields}}. The general runtime type-builder — constructs the `$`-key envelope dynamically (via assocRecord) since Fenel record literals can't carry a $-prefixed key.

std:charLt.label: Char less-than
std:charLt.description: True when char `a` orders before char `b` by Unicode code point. Char ordering reduces to numeric ordering of code points (Char = $opaque over codepoint). a/b are one-character strings (the Char runtime repr).

std:charCompare.label: Char compare
std:charCompare.description: Three-way compare of two chars by code point — -1 if a<b, 0 if equal, 1 if a>b.

std:strCompare.label: String compare
std:strCompare.description: Lexicographic three-way compare of two strings (the PURE source of truth for string ordering) — -1 if a<b, 0 if equal, 1 if a>b. Folds char-by-char (String = List Char) via `charCompare`; the first differing char decides, and a prefix orders before its extension (empty string is least).

std:strLt.label: String less-than
std:strLt.description: True when string `a` orders lexicographically before string `b`. The pure-Fenel definition (strCompare a b < 0); the `lt` native's both-strings branch is its opaque-repr perf shortcut.

std:natAdd.label: Nat add
std:natAdd.description: Peano addition over Nat = Zero | Succ. Structural recursion on the first operand: natAdd Zero b = b; natAdd (Succ p) b = Succ (natAdd p b). The pure source of truth for `add` at the Nat rung.

std:natMul.label: Nat multiply
std:natMul.description: Peano multiplication as repeated addition: natMul Zero b = Zero; natMul (Succ p) b = natAdd b (natMul p b). Composes natAdd.

std:natMonus.label: Nat monus
std:natMonus.description: Truncated subtraction (monus) — the Nat counterpart of `sub`: natMonus n Zero = n; natMonus Zero _ = Zero; natMonus (Succ p) (Succ q) = natMonus p q. Total (never negative); a-b clamps to Zero when b > a. Int (Phase 2) makes subtraction total/signed.

std:natLt.label: Nat less-than
std:natLt.description: Structural strict order over Nat: natLt a Zero = False; natLt Zero (Succ _) = True; natLt (Succ p) (Succ q) = natLt p q. Total (Nat order is decidable; the ℝ rung is where eq/lt go partial, D4).

std:natEq.label: Nat equal
std:natEq.description: Structural equality over Nat: both Zero ⇒ True; one Zero ⇒ False; both Succ ⇒ recurse on the predecessors. Total. The pure source of truth for `eq` at the Nat rung (the D6 String-typed native eq is fixed under the Eq class at Phase 5, not here).

std:natDiv.label: Nat divide
std:natDiv.description: Truncated (floor) division as repeated monus, guarded by natLt: natDiv a b = if a < b then Zero else Succ (natDiv (a - b) b). Zero divisor returns Zero (mirrors the native's zero-guard-to-0; the D7 law is asserted over the non-zero-divisor domain — the exact/refined-divisor semantics land at the Rational rung). Terminates by a well-founded Nat measure (the dividend strictly decreases while b >= 1) which is below the totality checker's structural/sub-1 rungs ⇒ checker returns Unknown, NOT @partial (the body IS total).

std:natMod.label: Nat modulo
std:natMod.description: Remainder via repeated monus, guarded by natLt: natMod a b = if a < b then a else natMod (a - b) b. Zero divisor returns a (keeps the div/mod identity a = b*(a/b) + a%b with natDiv a Zero = Zero; this DIVERGES from the native's zero-guard-to-0 — the documented zero-divisor carve-out, D7). Total by the same Nat measure as natDiv ⇒ checker Unknown, not @partial.

std:numberToNat.label: Number to Nat
std:numberToNat.description: Materialize a non-negative whole Number as a Peano Nat (Succ^n Zero). numberToNat n = if n <= 0 then Zero else Succ (numberToNat (n - 1)). For n <= 0 (and the fractional part of any non-integer) it returns the floor-clamped-to-Zero Peano value — the bridge is defined over the Nat domain [0,∞). Terminates by the guarded Number decrement (below the totality checker's Nat rungs ⇒ Unknown; total over the intended ℕ domain).

std:natToNumber.label: Nat to Number
std:natToNumber.description: Explicit approximate projection to finite Number. Its input refinement admits only values with a finite current projection; approximateNat returns a typed refusal otherwise. Exact arithmetic and text do not use this projection.

std:natToRefined.label: Nat to NonNegInt
std:natToRefined.description: Embed an exact Nat as the nonnegative Int refinement through all its integer digits. No Number projection occurs.

std:natFromRefined.label: NonNegInt to Nat
std:natFromRefined.description: Restore the exact nonnegative Int refinement as Nat through its integer digits. No Number projection occurs.

std:sameSign.label: Sign flags equal
std:sameSign.description: True when two `negative` sign flags agree (both negative or both non-negative). Helper for intAdd (same-sign test) and intEq. `sameSign a b = or (and a b) (and (not a) (not b))`.

std:xorSign.label: Sign flags xor
std:xorSign.description: Exclusive-or of two `negative` sign flags — the sign of a product (negative iff exactly one operand is negative). Helper for intMul. `xorSign a b = or (and a (not b)) (and (not a) b)`.

std:mkInt.label: Make Int
std:mkInt.description: The normalizing smart constructor — the negative-zero guard. mkInt m neg builds `Int { magnitude = m, negative = neg }` with the mathematical Bool flag, EXCEPT a Zero magnitude always yields `negative = False` (forcing +0). Every arithmetic result routes through mkInt so −0 is unrepresentable post-construction. Equality and order also handle raw pure constructor zero signs mathematically. An ordinary Fenel body — a case on the magnitude being Zero.

std:intNegate.label: Int negate
std:intNegate.description: Arithmetic negation — flip the sign flag through mkInt so −0 ⇒ +0: intNegate (Int m neg) = mkInt m (not neg). A tower op (the Nat rung has no negation; Int is the first SIGNED rung). Total.

std:intAdd.label: Int add
std:intAdd.description: Signed addition by case split on the operand signs. SAME sign ⇒ mkInt (natAdd |a| |b|) sign — add magnitudes, keep the shared sign. OPPOSITE sign ⇒ subtract the smaller magnitude from the larger with natMonus and take the LARGER's sign (natLt picks the larger). Equal opposite magnitudes ⇒ natMonus = Zero ⇒ mkInt forces +0 (no special case needed). Composes the Phase-1 Nat ops + mkInt.

std:intSub.label: Int subtract
std:intSub.description: Signed subtraction — now TOTAL (the Nat rung's natMonus truncated at Zero; Int is where subtraction becomes total/signed). intSub a b = intAdd a (intNegate b).

std:intMul.label: Int multiply
std:intMul.description: Signed multiplication — magnitude is natMul of the magnitudes, sign is the xor of the operand signs (negative iff exactly one is negative): mkInt (natMul |a| |b|) (xorSign n1 n2). A zero magnitude ⇒ natMul = Zero ⇒ mkInt forces +0 (so 0 × negative = +0). Composes natMul + mkInt.

std:intLt.label: Int less-than
std:intLt.description: Sign-aware strict order. A zero magnitude has a non-negative effective sign even when a raw pure constructor carries True. a negative, b non-negative ⇒ True; a non-negative, b negative ⇒ False; both non-negative ⇒ natLt of magnitudes; both negative ⇒ natLt REVERSED (−3 < −2 iff |−3| > |−2|). Total (Int order is decidable; the ℝ rung is where lt goes partial, D4).

std:intEq.label: Int equal
std:intEq.description: Mathematical equality — equal magnitudes and equal effective signs. Both zero magnitudes are equal regardless of the raw constructor's sign flag; nonzero magnitudes require matching signs. Total. The pure source of truth for `eq` at the Int rung.

std:numberToInt.label: Number to Int
std:numberToInt.description: Materialize a whole Number as a sign-magnitude Int: mkInt (numberToNat (abs n)) (lt n 0). The magnitude is the Peano materialization of |n|; the sign is (n < 0). numberToInt 0 ⇒ +0 (abs 0 = 0 ⇒ Zero magnitude ⇒ mkInt forces negative = False), so the bridge never emits −0. Defined over the ℤ domain (fractional parts floor-clamp through numberToNat).

std:intToNumber.label: Int to Number
std:intToNumber.description: Explicit approximate projection to finite Number. Its input refinement admits only values with a finite current projection; approximateInt returns a typed refusal otherwise. Exact arithmetic and text do not use this projection.

std:intToRefined.label: Int to integer-refinement
std:intToRefined.description: Normalize the same exact Int as its Integer refinement spelling. Every digit stays in the exact carrier; no Number projection occurs.

std:intFromRefined.label: Integer-refinement to Int
std:intFromRefined.description: Normalize the exact Integer refinement as Int without a Number projection.

std:natGcd.label: Nat gcd
std:natGcd.description: Greatest common divisor over Nat via Euclid's algorithm on natMod: natGcd a Zero = a; natGcd a (Succ q) = natGcd b (natMod a b). The new Nat op the lowest-terms reduction needs (mkRational divides num+den magnitudes by it). gcd is over Nat magnitudes — no signed remainder needed, so natMod suffices (no intMod). Terminates by the Nat measure (the second arg strictly decreases — natMod a b < b) which is below the totality checker's structural/sub-1 rungs ⇒ checker returns Unknown, NOT @partial (the body IS total; the natDiv/natMod precedent).

std:mkRational.label: Make Rational
std:mkRational.description: Normalize two Int parts: put the sign in the numerator, divide by their gcd, and use 0/1 for zero. This unchecked reference constructor retains its historical zero-denominator sentinel; public rationalFromParts refuses zero before calling it. Every arithmetic output is reduced with a positive denominator.

std:ratNeg.label: Rational negate
std:ratNeg.description: Arithmetic negation — negate the numerator (an Int) through mkRational; the denominator is unchanged. ratNeg (Rational num den) = mkRational (intNegate num) (mkInt den False). Total (the den Nat lifts to a positive Int via mkInt). Routing through mkRational preserves the canonical form (den already coprime ⇒ a re-reduce by gcd 1).

std:ratAdd.label: Rational add
std:ratAdd.description: a/b + c/d = (a·d + c·b)/(b·d). Numerator = intAdd (intMul aNum |bDen|) (intMul bNum |aDen|); denominator = natMul aDen bDen (lifted to a positive Int); through mkRational (which reduces to lowest terms — cross-multiplication is NOT already reduced). The dens (Nat) lift to positive Ints via mkInt _ False. Composes the Phase-2 Int ops + the Phase-1 Nat ops + mkRational.

std:ratSub.label: Rational subtract
std:ratSub.description: ratSub a b = ratAdd a (ratNeg b). Total.

std:ratMul.label: Rational multiply
std:ratMul.description: (a/b)·(c/d) = (a·c)/(b·d). mkRational (intMul aNum bNum) (natMul aDen bDen lifted to a positive Int). Through mkRational so e.g. (2/3)·(3/4) = 6/12 reduces to 1/2. Composes intMul + natMul + mkRational.

std:ratDiv.label: Rational divide
std:ratDiv.description: (a/b)÷(c/d) = (a·d)/(b·c). mkRational (intMul aNum |bDen|) (intMul |aDen| bNum). This is WHY mkRational takes a SIGNED Int denominator: b's numerator sign + zero-ness flow through the one mkRational guard. bNum = 0 ⇒ the denominator magnitude is Zero ⇒ mkRational hits its zero-den guard ⇒ the documented 0/1 sentinel (the rational div-by-zero boundary, the Nat zero-divisor precedent).

std:ratEq.label: Rational equal
std:ratEq.description: Exact mathematical equality by cross multiplication. Positive denominators make 1/2 and 2/4 equal even before checked construction normalizes their representation.

std:ratLt.label: Rational less-than
std:ratLt.description: Cross-multiplied strict order: a/b < c/d iff a·d < c·b (both dens positive ⇒ the inequality direction is preserved). intLt (intMul aNum |bDen|) (intMul bNum |aDen|). The dens lift to positive Ints via mkInt _ False. Total (Rational order is decidable; the ℝ rung is where lt goes partial, D4).

std:rationalToNumber.label: Rational to Number
std:rationalToNumber.description: Explicit approximate Rational-to-Number projection. Fractions can lose digits in the double; approximateRational adds a checked finite-result boundary. Exact runtime/storage Reprable uses integer strings instead.

std:numberToRational.label: Number to Rational
std:numberToRational.description: Materialize an integer-domain Number as the pure Rational n/1 through the existing Int/Nat bridges. This is a small pure-sample bridge, not exact decimal input or the default Reprable crossing; parseRational reads digits directly.

std:ratToRefined.label: Rational to ℚ-refinement
std:ratToRefined.description: Normalize an exact Rational into its ℚ-refinement spelling. Every fraction and integer digit stays in the same exact representation.

std:ratFromRefined.label: ℚ-refinement to Rational
std:ratFromRefined.description: Normalize the exact ℚ-refinement spelling as Rational; no Number projection occurs.

std:natMax.label: Nat max
std:natMax.description: The larger of two Nats: natMax a b = if natLt a b then b else a. The new Nat op the Real modulus combinators need (the modulus of a+b/a*b takes the max of the operands' moduli at a shifted precision). Homed in the real module to keep nat-arith.fenel frozen (the natGcd-in-rational precedent). Total.

std:ratEps2.label: Combined error bound 2/(k+1)
std:ratEps2.description: The combined-error Rational 2/(k+1) at precision k = mkRational 2 (k+1), built via the NUMBER BRIDGES (numberToInt over add (natToNumber k) 1) rather than Succ-literals. WHY THE BRIDGE PATH: feeding a Succ-literal-built or mkInt-built Nat/Int (e.g. `mkInt (Succ k) False`) into mkRational — which runs natGcd/natDiv on it — triggers an engine evaluation blow-up (Maximum-call-stack; see the roadmap Phase-4 surprises), whereas numberToInt/numberToNat-built values feed the deep arithmetic recursion cleanly. So eps2 routes k through the bridge (Nat → Number → Int) — robust + still exact for the small k a fuel-bounded search reaches. The Real comparison separation test declares two reals separated when their sampled approximations differ by more than this. Decreases toward 0 linearly (the 1/(k+1) modulus convention).

std:realNegate.label: Real negate
std:realNegate.description: Arithmetic negation, pointwise: (−a).seq n = ratNeg (a.seq n); the modulus is UNCHANGED (|−x − −y| = |x − y|). TOTAL. converges is the Axiom-discharged stub CauchyAx (the proof that ratNeg preserves Cauchy-ness with the same modulus is stated, not kernel-checked this phase).

std:realAdd.label: Real add
std:realAdd.description: Addition, pointwise: (a+b).seq n = ratAdd (a.seq n) (b.seq n). MODULUS: to get the sum within 1/2^k, each summand must be within 1/2^(k+1), so (a+b).modulus k = natMax (a.modulus (Succ k)) (b.modulus (Succ k)) — the standard constructive-reals additive modulus. TOTAL. Composes ratAdd + natMax. converges = CauchyAx (stub).

std:realSub.label: Real subtract
std:realSub.description: realSub a b = realAdd a (realNegate b). TOTAL.

std:realMul.label: Real multiply
std:realMul.description: Multiplication, pointwise: (a·b).seq n = ratMul (a.seq n) (b.seq n). MODULUS — STUB (flagged): a RIGOROUS multiplication modulus depends on the operands' MAGNITUDE bounds (to bound the product error |a·Δb + b·Δa| one needs N with 2^N ≥ |a|,|b|), which requires materializing magnitude bounds the kernel `converges` proof would carry. This phase uses the same conservative additive-shape modulus as realAdd — natMax (a.modulus (Succ k)) (b.modulus (Succ k)) — which is SOUND for the bounded-magnitude reals the tests exercise; the rigorous magnitude-aware modulus is DEFERRED alongside the kernel convergence proof (numeric-tower Phase 4 fence §3). TOTAL. Composes ratMul + natMax.

std:realSampleAt.label: Real sample-at
std:realSampleAt.description: Sample a Real's approximating sequence at precision k: realSampleAt r k = r.seq (r.modulus k) — the rational approximation guaranteed within 1/2^k of the limit. THE fundamental observation of a real (the comparison search + the realToNumber projection both sample through it).

std:sepDecision.label: Separation decision
std:sepDecision.description: The per-precision 3-way separation decision over two sampled approximations pa, pb and the combined error bound eps2 = 2/2^k. If pa + eps2 < pb ⇒ the operands are definitively separated, first below second ⇒ Just True. If pb + eps2 < pa ⇒ separated, first above second ⇒ Just False. Otherwise the samples overlap within the combined error (cannot separate at this precision) ⇒ Nothing. SOUND — a Just is returned only with a genuine gap exceeding the combined sampling error.

std:realSeparate.label: Real separate
std:realSeparate.description: The comparison workhorse: search for a SEPARATION WITNESS between a and b, from precision k, within a fuel budget. At each precision k take sepDecision (realSampleAt a k) (realSampleAt b k) (ratEps2 k): a Just is a witness (Just True = a<b, Just False = a>b) returned immediately; a Nothing means the samples still overlap, so increase precision (Succ k), consume one fuel, and retry. Fuel exhausted (Zero) ⇒ Nothing (cannot decide within budget — NOT a wrong answer; includes the genuinely-equal case). Recurses STRUCTURALLY on fuel ⇒ total (the partiality is in the Maybe codomain, not termination).

std:realLt.label: Real less-than (partial)
std:realLt.description: realLt a b fuel : Maybe Bool — strict order with an explicit Nat fuel budget. Delegates to realSeparate from precision Zero: Just True when a is witnessed below b within budget, Just False when a is witnessed above b, Nothing when the budget is exhausted without separation (the honest decidability boundary — real order is only SEMI-decidable). The FIRST typed-partial order op in the tower (Rational lt and below stay TOTAL). The fuel is explicit on the body; the call boundary supplies a sensible default.

std:realEq.label: Real equal (partial)
std:realEq.description: realEq a b fuel : Maybe Bool — equality with an explicit Nat fuel budget. Equality is NEVER positively confirmable by finite sampling (the sequences could agree arbitrarily long then diverge), so this is SOUND-conservative: if a and b SEPARATE within budget (realSeparate returns Just _, either direction), they are unequal ⇒ Just False; otherwise ⇒ Nothing (cannot confirm equality). It NEVER returns Just True — the degenerate definitional Just-True (syntactic identity) is omitted as a deliberate soundness choice (never a Just we cannot witness). Nothing IS the decidability boundary as a value (D4/north-star §6).

std:ratToReal.label: Rational to Real
std:ratToReal.description: The ℚ↪ℝ embedding: a Real whose value is the Rational q, as the CONSTANT sequence seq n = q with modulus k = Zero (every term is the limit ⇒ trivially Cauchy, modulus 0). The principled Real constructor (matches the SUBTYPE_LATTICE Rational⊂Real row); numberToReal and the tests build reals from it. converges = CauchyAx (the constant-sequence convergence is the simplest discharge).

std:numberToReal.label: Number to Real
std:numberToReal.description: Materialize a Number as a Real via the rational embedding: numberToReal x = ratToReal (numberToRational x). Faithful over the integer Number domain (numberToRational floors fractional parts — the Phase-3 bridge contract; non-integer reals are constructed with ratToReal over an exact Rational). The LOWER of the Reprable JsRuntime/Jsonb Real instances.

std:realToNumber.label: Real to Number
std:realToNumber.description: Sample a Real to a Number (the LOSSY projection, the D7 ℝ carve-out): realToNumber r = rationalToNumber (r.seq (r.modulus PREC)) at a fixed precision PREC = 30 (≈ 2^30 ≈ 1e9, ~double precision). For a constant-sequence (ratToReal / numberToReal) real the modulus is Zero so the sample is the exact embedded Rational; for an arithmetic result the modulus selects the sampling index. The LIFT of the Reprable JsRuntime/Jsonb Real instances — a Number is a SAMPLE of the real at one precision, never an exact round-trippable rep (unlike the finite rungs).

std:realToRefined.label: Real to ℝ-refinement
std:realToRefined.description: Iso witness (D8): the Real ⇄ ℝ refinement view. realToRefined = realToNumber re-typed onto the real refinement of Number. CODOMAIN CLOSED (containment-substrate Phase 3): the precise codomain `RealNumber = Number | value ∈ ℝ` is now a registered alias (foundation.fenel; ℝ = membershipReal, the finite reals — a mild PROPER refinement, not bare identity). This is the FIRST rung where the inductive↔refinement presentations diverge in decidability (Cauchy eq partial; ℝ interval membership Tri-partial). Pairs with realFromRefined; round-trips over the exact-sample sub-domain (sample-discharged Phase 4, $el law field Phase 5).

std:realFromRefined.label: ℝ-refinement to Real
std:realFromRefined.description: Iso witness (D8): the inverse of realToRefined. realFromRefined = numberToReal over the real-refined domain `RealNumber = Number | value ∈ ℝ` (CLOSED, containment-substrate Phase 3; see realToRefined). Pairs with realToRefined.

std:natEqM.label: Nat eq (Maybe)
std:natEqM.description: Decidable Nat equality, Just-wrapped for the Eq Nat instance: natEqM a b = Just (natEq a b). Always Just (Nat equality is total).

std:natNeqM.label: Nat neq (Maybe)
std:natNeqM.description: Decidable Nat inequality: natNeqM a b = Just (not (natEq a b)). Always Just.

std:natLtM.label: Nat lt (Maybe)
std:natLtM.description: Decidable Nat strict order: natLtM a b = Just (natLt a b). Always Just.

std:natLteM.label: Nat lte (Maybe)
std:natLteM.description: Decidable Nat ≤: natLteM a b = Just (or (natLt a b) (natEq a b)). Always Just.

std:natGtM.label: Nat gt (Maybe)
std:natGtM.description: Decidable Nat >: natGtM a b = Just (natLt b a) (flip lt). Always Just.

std:natGteM.label: Nat gte (Maybe)
std:natGteM.description: Decidable Nat ≥: natGteM a b = Just (or (natLt b a) (natEq a b)). Always Just.

std:intEqM.label: Int eq (Maybe)
std:intEqM.description: Decidable Int equality, Just-wrapped: intEqM a b = Just (intEq a b).

std:intNeqM.label: Int neq (Maybe)
std:intNeqM.description: Decidable Int inequality: intNeqM a b = Just (not (intEq a b)).

std:intLtM.label: Int lt (Maybe)
std:intLtM.description: Decidable Int strict order: intLtM a b = Just (intLt a b).

std:intLteM.label: Int lte (Maybe)
std:intLteM.description: Decidable Int ≤: intLteM a b = Just (or (intLt a b) (intEq a b)).

std:intGtM.label: Int gt (Maybe)
std:intGtM.description: Decidable Int >: intGtM a b = Just (intLt b a).

std:intGteM.label: Int gte (Maybe)
std:intGteM.description: Decidable Int ≥: intGteM a b = Just (or (intLt b a) (intEq b a)).

std:ratEqM.label: Rational eq (Maybe)
std:ratEqM.description: Decidable Rational equality, Just-wrapped: ratEqM a b = Just (ratEq a b).

std:ratNeqM.label: Rational neq (Maybe)
std:ratNeqM.description: Decidable Rational inequality: ratNeqM a b = Just (not (ratEq a b)).

std:ratLtM.label: Rational lt (Maybe)
std:ratLtM.description: Decidable Rational strict order: ratLtM a b = Just (ratLt a b).

std:ratLteM.label: Rational lte (Maybe)
std:ratLteM.description: Decidable Rational ≤: ratLteM a b = Just (or (ratLt a b) (ratEq a b)).

std:ratGtM.label: Rational gt (Maybe)
std:ratGtM.description: Decidable Rational >: ratGtM a b = Just (ratLt b a).

std:ratGteM.label: Rational gte (Maybe)
std:ratGteM.description: Decidable Rational ≥: ratGteM a b = Just (or (ratLt b a) (ratEq a b)).

std:negateMB.label: Negate a Maybe Bool
std:negateMB.description: negateMB m = case m of Nothing -> Nothing | Just x -> Just (not x). Lifts boolean negation through the decidability Maybe — Nothing (undecided) stays Nothing, a decided Just flips. Used by the ℝ neq/lte/gte wrappers (≤ via ¬(b<a)).

std:realEqDefault.label: Real eq (default fuel)
std:realEqDefault.description: realEqDefault a b = realEq a b (numberToNat 64) : Maybe Bool. SOUND-conservative — Just False on separation, Nothing when equality is undecided within budget (NEVER Just True; real equality is not positively confirmable). The Eq Real instance's eq.

std:realNeqDefault.label: Real neq (default fuel)
std:realNeqDefault.description: realNeqDefault a b = negateMB (realEqDefault a b). Just True on separation, Nothing when undecided. The Eq Real instance's neq.

std:realLtDefault.label: Real lt (default fuel)
std:realLtDefault.description: realLtDefault a b = realLt a b (numberToNat 64) : Maybe Bool. Just True/False on a separation witness, Nothing when undecided within budget. The Ord Real instance's lt.

std:realGtDefault.label: Real gt (default fuel)
std:realGtDefault.description: realGtDefault a b = realLt b a (numberToNat 64) (flip lt). The Ord Real instance's gt.

std:realLteDefault.label: Real lte (default fuel)
std:realLteDefault.description: realLteDefault a b = negateMB (realLt b a (numberToNat 64)) — a ≤ b ⟺ ¬(b < a), lifted through the decidability Maybe (Nothing stays Nothing). The Ord Real instance's lte.

std:realGteDefault.label: Real gte (default fuel)
std:realGteDefault.description: realGteDefault a b = negateMB (realLt a b (numberToNat 64)) — a ≥ b ⟺ ¬(a < b). The Ord Real instance's gte.

std:towerToDouble.label: Tower to double
std:towerToDouble.description: The Reprable Number LIFT (pure tagged-variant → native double): collapse a tagged tower value to the flat JS double via each rung's own *ToNumber bridge. towerToDouble n = case n of NatN x -> natToNumber x | IntN x -> intToNumber x | RatN x -> rationalToNumber x | RealN x -> realToNumber x. TOTAL + exact (RealN is the lossy rung — a sample, the D7 ℝ carve-out). The PERF direction (the double is the IEEE fast path).

std:doubleToTower.label: Double to tower
std:doubleToTower.description: The Reprable Number LOWER (native double → pure tagged-variant): tag a flat JS double. doubleToTower d = if eq d (floor d) then IntN (numberToInt d) else RealN (numberToReal d). INTEGRAL ⇒ IntN, else RealN — lower NEVER produces NatN/RatN (FORK-2: no finite test recovers ℕ⊂ℤ or a non-integer's exact rung; the double lost the tag — the lossy-but-total carve-out). The REASONING direction (materialise a rung from the perf rep).

std:intEnumFromTo.label: Int enumFromTo
std:intEnumFromTo.description: The `Enumerable Int` step: the bounded integer range [lo..hi] inclusive as a pure cons-spine `List Int`. intEnumFromTo lo hi = if intLt hi lo then Nil else Cons lo (intEnumFromTo (intAdd lo (numberToInt 1)) hi). The step unit is built via numberToInt 1 (the bridge path, not a Succ-literal — the numeric-tower §0.2 stack hazard); intAdd/intLt compose the Phase-2 Int bodies. lo > hi ⇒ Nil (empty range); lo == hi ⇒ a singleton. Total over the bounded-interval domain (recurses on the shrinking hi − lo measure; the totality checker returns Unknown — the natDiv precedent).

std:natEnumFromTo.label: Nat enumFromTo
std:natEnumFromTo.description: The `Enumerable Nat` step: the bounded Peano range [lo..hi] inclusive as a pure cons-spine `List Nat`, stepping by Succ. natEnumFromTo lo hi = if natLt hi lo then Nil else Cons lo (natEnumFromTo (Succ lo) hi). Pure Peano successor stepping (no bridge needed — Succ is the Nat successor; natLt is shallow/structural per step, NOT the natMul recursion the §0.2 hazard names). lo > hi ⇒ Nil. Total over the bounded range (recurses on the shrinking hi − lo measure; Unknown to the totality checker).

std:charEnumFromTo.label: Char enumFromTo
std:charEnumFromTo.description: The `Enumerable Char` step: the bounded codepoint range [lo..hi] inclusive as a pure cons-spine `List Char`, stepping by the next Unicode codepoint. charEnumFromTo lo hi = if gt (charCode lo) (charCode hi) then Nil else Cons lo (charEnumFromTo (charFromCode (add (charCode lo) 1)) hi). Composes the host leaves charCode/charFromCode (NO new leaf); the order is by codepoint (charCode), exactly as charLt orders Chars. lo > hi (by codepoint) ⇒ Nil; lo == hi ⇒ singleton. Total over the bounded range (recurses on the shrinking codepoint gap; the totality checker returns Unknown — the intEnumFromTo precedent).

std:listToArray.label: List to array
std:listToArray.description: Fold a pure cons-spine List into its native array repr (the Reprable JsRuntime (List a) LIFT). listToArray Nil = []; listToArray (Cons h t) = concat [h] (listToArray t). Element-transparent — each head rides through untouched. Structural recursion on the spine ⇒ terminates; below the totality checker's List rungs (Unknown), total over the intended List domain.

std:arrayToList.label: Array to list
std:arrayToList.description: Fold a native array into the pure cons-spine List (the Reprable JsRuntime (List a) LOWER). arrayToList walks the array with the head/drop natives: empty ⇒ Nil; else Cons (head) (arrayToList (drop 1)). Element-transparent — each element rides through untouched. Recurses on the strictly-shorter `drop 1` tail ⇒ terminates over the finite array domain.

std:stringToCharList.label: String to char list
std:stringToCharList.description: Split a JS string into a pure cons-spine List of Char (the Reprable JsRuntime String LOWER). stringToCharList = arrayToList ∘ chars: `chars` splits by Unicode code point (emoji/non-BMP stay grouped, each element a 1-char String = Char's runtime repr), then the List lower folds the array into the cons-spine. Reuses the List spine bridge — String is List Char with a flat-string native.

std:charListToString.label: Char list to string
std:charListToString.description: Fold a pure cons-spine List of Char back into a JS string (the Reprable JsRuntime String LIFT). charListToString = join (listToArray cs) "": the List lift folds the cons-spine into an array of 1-char Strings (Char's runtime repr), then `join … ""` concatenates. The inverse of stringToCharList over the BMP + grouped-codepoint domain `chars` defines.

std:minimum.label: Minimum
std:minimum.description: List minimum — the smallest element by natural ordering, or Nothing. ∀a. List a → Maybe a. Nothing for the empty list (no extremum of ∅) AND for any list carrying a pair the ordering leaf cannot compare — mixed number/string, or a homogeneous list of booleans/records/lists (only number/number and string/string are ordered). A singleton is its own extremum under any order, so `[x]` ⇒ `Just x` for every x. Compare with `min`, which is binary and Number-typed. signature-substrate slice 3c-D2 repaired this from `List a -> a` returning host-`undefined`, which violated SC-sig.

std:maximum.label: Maximum
std:maximum.description: List maximum — the largest element by natural ordering, or Nothing. ∀a. List a → Maybe a. Nothing for the empty list AND for any list carrying a pair the ordering leaf cannot compare — mixed number/string, or a homogeneous list of booleans/records/lists (only number/number and string/string are ordered). A singleton is its own extremum under any order, so `[x]` ⇒ `Just x` for every x. Compare with `max`, which is binary and Number-typed. signature-substrate slice 3c-D2 repaired this from `List a -> a` returning host-`undefined`, which violated SC-sig.

std:minimumScan.label: Minimum scan
std:minimumScan.description: The running fold behind `minimum`: `acc` is Nothing before the first element is seen and Just-the-running-minimum afterwards. Returns Nothing the moment a pair is not orderable, which is what short-circuits the unsupported-comparison fence. Ties keep the EARLIER element (strict `lt`), matching the pre-repair native. Internal helper.

std:maximumScan.label: Maximum scan
std:maximumScan.description: The running fold behind `maximum`: `acc` is Nothing before the first element is seen and Just-the-running-maximum afterwards. Returns Nothing the moment a pair is not orderable. Ties keep the EARLIER element (strict `gt`), matching the pre-repair native. Internal helper.

std:orderablePair.label: Orderable pair
std:orderablePair.description: True iff the ordering leaf can compare these two values: both numbers, or both strings. Every other pairing — mixed number/string, two booleans, two records, two lists — is NOT orderable, and `minimum`/`maximum` fence to Nothing rather than guess. This mirrors the `lt`/`gt` natives exactly: they return False (not an ordering) for every pair outside those two kinds, so without this guard a fold over them would silently report the first element as the extremum.

std:map.label: Map
std:map.description: Apply a function to each element. ∀a b. (a → b) → List a → List b

std:filter.label: Filter
std:filter.description: Keep elements where predicate is true. ∀a. (a → Bool) → List a → List a

std:fold.label: Fold
std:fold.description: Reduce list to a single value (left fold). ∀a b. (b → a → b) → b → List a → b

std:flatMap.label: Flat map
std:flatMap.description: Map then flatten. ∀a b. (a → List b) → List a → List b

std:find.label: Find
std:find.description: First element matching predicate. Nothing if none match. ∀a. (a → Bool) → List a → Maybe a

std:findIndexAt.label: Find index (from)
std:findIndexAt.description: Index-threading helper for findIndex: the index of the first predicate match at or after position i, or -1. Internal recursion carrier — keeps findIndex's public signature clean while the recursion short-circuits like the native.

std:findIndex.label: Find index
std:findIndex.description: Index of the first element matching predicate, or -1 when no match. ∀a. (a → Bool) → List a → Int

std:all.label: All
std:all.description: Do all elements satisfy the predicate? True on the empty list. Short-circuits on the first failure. ∀a. List a → (a → Bool) → Bool

std:some.label: Some
std:some.description: Does any element satisfy the predicate? False on the empty list. Short-circuits on the first hit. ∀a. List a → (a → Bool) → Bool

std:none.label: None
std:none.description: Does no element satisfy the predicate? True on the empty list. Short-circuits on the first hit. ∀a. List a → (a → Bool) → Bool

std:takeWhile.label: Take while
std:takeWhile.description: Take elements while predicate holds. ∀a. (a → Bool) → List a → List a

std:dropWhile.label: Drop while
std:dropWhile.description: Drop elements while predicate holds. ∀a. (a → Bool) → List a → List a

std:zipWith.label: Zip with
std:zipWith.description: Combine corresponding pairs. ∀a b c. (a → b → c) → List a → List b → List c

std:partition.label: Partition
std:partition.description: Split list into [matching, non-matching] by predicate. ∀a. (a → Bool) → List a → (List a, List a)

std:groupByAcc.label: Group by (accumulate)
std:groupByAcc.description: Forward accumulator for groupBy: thread the groups record left-to-right so group keys appear in first-encounter order and elements append in list order — exactly the native's insertion-order semantics. Internal helper.

std:groupBy.label: Group by
std:groupBy.description: Group elements by key function. ∀a b. (a → b) → List a → Record b (List a)

std:sortDecorate.label: Sort decorate
std:sortDecorate.description: Decorate every element with its sort key: { k = key x, v = x } per element, invoking the key exactly ONCE per element (as the native does). Internal helper for sort.

std:sortMergeHead.label: Sort merge head
std:sortMergeHead.description: Consume one original head-to-head merge decision, leaving empty runs untouched. Internal helper for sort.

std:sortMergeSteps.label: Sort merge steps
std:sortMergeSteps.description: Consume at most the requested number of head-to-head merge decisions, returning the merged prefix and remaining runs. Binary steps keep authored recursion logarithmic without assuming a total key order. Internal helper for sort.

std:sortMergePairs.label: Sort merge pairs
std:sortMergePairs.description: Stable merge of two key-decorated runs: the right head goes first only when its key is lt the left head's; ties and incomparable keys keep encounter order (left first) — the stability half of the merge sort. Internal helper for sort.

std:sortPairs.label: Sort pairs
std:sortPairs.description: Stable merge sort over key-decorated pairs: split at half, recurse, merge (sortMergePairs). Internal helper for sort.

std:sortUndecorate.label: Sort undecorate
std:sortUndecorate.description: Recover sorted elements from decorated pairs with binary splits, keeping authored recursion logarithmic. Internal helper for sort.

std:sort.label: Sort
std:sort.description: Sort list ascending by key function, stably. Keys std lt cannot compare (across types, Bools, records, NaN) are a tie and keep encounter order. ∀a b. (a → b) → List a → List a

std:compose.label: Compose
std:compose.description: Compose two callables: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). ∀a b c. (b → c) → (a → b) → (a → c)

std:flip.label: Flip
std:flip.description: Swap argument order of a 2-arg function. ∀a b c. (a → b → c) → (b → a → c)

std:assocRecord.label: Assoc record
std:assocRecord.description: Set a dynamic key on a record, returning a new record. ∀a. Record String a → String → a → Record String a. Mirrors `{...record, [key]: value}` in JS. Sister of std:entries — Phase 13a sub-step 2 added this to retire the 12d-7 wrapper-side applyMapping iteration (the handle-platform branch needed dynamic key construction). Also retires one of the 12c-core deferred follow-ups.

std:at.label: At
std:at.description: Get the raw element at index `n`. Negative indices count from the end. This is a partial native: out-of-range returns the runtime null sentinel, so typed callers must prove bounds before consuming the result. ∀a. List a → Number → a

std:concat.label: Concat
std:concat.description: Concatenate two lists. ∀a. List a → List a → List a — equivalent to Haskell `++`. The JS performance leaf retains a legacy two-string representation arm, but String remains nominal and inferred String construction uses the exact `join : List String → String → String` surface.

std:distinctCount.label: Distinct count
std:distinctCount.description: Number of distinct elements in a list under ordinary structural `eq`: `length (unique arr)`. NaN is never equal to itself, so every NaN counts; closures count by identity. ∀a. Eq a => List a → ℕ.

std:drop.label: Drop
std:drop.description: Skip the first n elements. ∀a. ℕ → List a → List a

std:flatten.label: Flatten
std:flatten.description: Flatten nested lists by one level. ∀a. List (List a) → List a

std:head.label: Head
std:head.description: First element of a list (or first character of a string). ∀a. List a → Maybe a

std:includes.label: Includes
std:includes.description: Does the list contain an element `eq` to the value? Structural: separately built constructors, records and JSON round trips are found; NaN is never found (NaN ≠ NaN); closures compare by identity. A non-list (a String included) contains nothing. ∀a. List a → a → Bool

std:init.label: Init
std:init.description: All elements except the last. ∀a. List a → Maybe (List a)

std:last.label: Last
std:last.description: Last element of a list (or last character of a string). ∀a. List a → Maybe a

std:lookup.label: Lookup
std:lookup.description: Look up a dynamic key on a record. Returns Just<value> when present (regardless of value-truthiness — empty strings + 0 + false return Just), Nothing when the key is missing. ∀a. Record String a → String → Maybe a. Sister of std:assocRecord — Phase 13a sub-step 2 added this to retire the 12d-7 wrapper-side row[csvCol] dynamic-field read. Also retires one of the 12c-core deferred follow-ups.

std:mergeRecords.label: Merge records
std:mergeRecords.description: Shallow merge of two records into a new record. Fields from `b` overwrite fields from `a` on key collision (right-biased) — mirrors `{...a, ...b}` in JS / `M.union` in Haskell. Used when an orchestration body needs to extend a base payload with caller-provided extras.

std:reverse.label: Reverse
std:reverse.description: Reverse list order. ∀a. List a → List a

std:sortLex.label: Sort lex
std:sortLex.description: Sort a list of strings ascending in lexicographic (default JS string compare) order. ∀. List String → List String. The JS-native sort is stable, so equal elements preserve insertion order. Phase 21.2 introduced this as a no-key-fn alternative to `sort id …` — `sort` takes a key-function arg whose closure-conversion-in-compiled-targets is gappy on the self-host substrate, while `sortLex` is a single-arg native that lowers to a direct runtime helper call.

std:tail.label: Tail
std:tail.description: All elements except the first. ∀a. List a → Maybe (List a)

std:take.label: Take
std:take.description: Take the first n elements. ∀a. ℕ → List a → List a

std:unique.label: Unique
std:unique.description: Remove duplicates under ordinary structural `eq`, keeping each first occurrence in order. NaN is never equal to itself, so every NaN is kept; closures compare by identity. A non-list (a String included) gives the empty list. ∀a. List a → List a

std:zip.label: Zip
std:zip.description: Pair corresponding elements. ∀a b. List a → List b → List (a, b)

std:addDays.label: Add days
std:addDays.description: Add n days to a date

std:addHours.label: Add hours
std:addHours.description: Add n hours to a date

std:diffDays.label: Diff days
std:diffDays.description: Number of days between two dates

std:formatDate.label: Format date
std:formatDate.description: Format date as string (ISO, short, long)

std:namedSet.label: Named SetExpr
std:namedSet.description: Reference a registered named set (NAMED_SETS) by name as a SetExpr value `{$ref: name}`. Irreducible host bridge — Fenel record literals can't author a `$`-prefixed key. String → SetExpr.

std:regexSet.label: Regex → SetExpr
std:regexSet.description: Parse a regular-expression string into a SetExpr (algebraic Pattern under `$pattern`). Irreducible host leaf delegating to the engine's `regexStringToPattern`; throws on the (unreachable for real input) malformed case so a bad curated rule fails loud at boot. String → SetExpr.

std:imageBlueChannel.label: Blue channel
std:imageBlueChannel.description: Keep blue, zero red and green.

std:imageBoxBlur.label: Box blur
std:imageBoxBlur.description: Average each RGB pixel with its (2·radius+1)² neighbors, clamping edges and retaining the pixel's alpha. Radius zero preserves the image. Cheaper but boxier than Gaussian.

std:imageBrightness.label: Brightness
std:imageBrightness.description: Add `delta` to each RGB component (clamped to 0..255). Negative darkens, positive lightens.

std:imageContrast.label: Contrast
std:imageContrast.description: Scale each component around 128: (px−128)·factor + 128. factor>1 boosts, <1 flattens.

std:imageCrop.label: Crop
std:imageCrop.description: Extract a sub-rectangle starting at (x, y) with the given width and height. Out-of-bounds is clipped.

std:imageDifference.label: Difference
std:imageDifference.description: Absolute per-channel difference: |a − b|. Useful for change detection.

std:imageDither.label: Dither (Floyd-Steinberg)
std:imageDither.description: Floyd-Steinberg error diffusion to monochrome. Distributes quantization error to neighboring pixels.

std:imageEdgeDetect.label: Edge detect (Sobel)
std:imageEdgeDetect.description: Sobel operator on the grayscale projection — outputs gradient magnitude as light edges on a dark background.

std:imageEmboss.label: Emboss
std:imageEmboss.description: Convolve with the standard emboss kernel — gives a directional bas-relief look.

std:imageGamma.label: Gamma
std:imageGamma.description: Gamma correction: out = 255·(in/255)^(1/gamma). gamma>1 brightens midtones, <1 darkens.

std:imageGaussianBlur.label: Gaussian blur
std:imageGaussianBlur.description: Convolve RGB with a Gaussian kernel of size 2·radius+1 (sigma = radius/2), clamping edges and retaining each pixel's alpha. Radius zero preserves the image. Smooth, isotropic blur.

std:imageGradient.label: Gradient
std:imageGradient.description: Horizontal linear gradient between two colors.

std:imageGrayscale.label: Grayscale
std:imageGrayscale.description: Convert each pixel to grayscale via the Rec. 601 luminance formula (0.299·R + 0.587·G + 0.114·B). Alpha preserved.

std:imageGreenChannel.label: Green channel
std:imageGreenChannel.description: Keep green, zero red and blue.

std:imageHueRotate.label: Hue rotate
std:imageHueRotate.description: Rotate each pixel's hue by `degrees` (0..360) in HSL space.

std:imageInvert.label: Invert colors
std:imageInvert.description: Invert each pixel's RGB: R→255−R, G→255−G, B→255−B. Alpha preserved.

std:imageMedian.label: Median
std:imageMedian.description: Replace each pixel with the median of its (2·radius+1)² neighborhood. Strong denoise, preserves edges.

std:imageMultiply.label: Multiply blend
std:imageMultiply.description: Per-pixel multiply blend: result = a·b/255. Always darkens.

std:imageNoise.label: Noise
std:imageNoise.description: Deterministic monochrome white noise (Mulberry32 PRNG seeded by `seed`).

std:imageOverlay.label: Overlay
std:imageOverlay.description: Source-over composite straight RGBA pixels, accounting for both alpha channels. Output dimensions are bottom's; pixels outside top are retained. Fully transparent overlaps normalize to transparent black.

std:imagePixelate.label: Pixelate
std:imagePixelate.description: Average each `factor`×`factor` block into a single color. factor=1 is a no-op; larger factors produce blockier output.

std:imagePosterize.label: Posterize
std:imagePosterize.description: Quantize each channel to `levels` evenly-spaced steps. Lower levels produce a flatter, banded look.

std:imageRedChannel.label: Red channel
std:imageRedChannel.description: Keep red, zero green and blue.

std:imageResize.label: Resize
std:imageResize.description: Resample to a new width × height using bilinear interpolation.

std:imageRotate180.label: Rotate 180°
std:imageRotate180.description: Rotate by 180 degrees — same as flipping both axes.

std:imageRotate90.label: Rotate 90°
std:imageRotate90.description: Rotate clockwise by 90 degrees. Width and height swap.

std:imageSample.label: Bundled sample
std:imageSample.description: Return one of the bundled sample images by index. Use this in saved expressions instead of embedding pixel literals — same expressions stay small and human-readable.

std:imageSaturate.label: Saturate
std:imageSaturate.description: Scale saturation in HSL space. factor=0 is grayscale, 1 is identity, >1 oversaturates.

std:imageScreen.label: Screen
std:imageScreen.description: Per-pixel screen blend: result = 255 − (255−a)(255−b)/255. Always lightens.

std:imageSepia.label: Sepia
std:imageSepia.description: Apply the standard sepia tone matrix — warm reddish-brown tint reminiscent of aged photos.

std:imageSharpen.label: Sharpen
std:imageSharpen.description: Convolve with the classic 5-center sharpen kernel — boosts the difference between each pixel and its 4 neighbors.

std:imageSolid.label: Solid
std:imageSolid.description: Fresh image of a single solid color.

std:imageSwapRedBlue.label: Swap R↔B
std:imageSwapRedBlue.description: Swap the red and blue channels — useful for converting BGR ↔ RGB byte order.

std:imageSwapRedGreen.label: Swap R↔G
std:imageSwapRedGreen.description: Swap the red and green channels.

std:imageThreshold.label: Threshold
std:imageThreshold.description: Binarize on luminance: pixels below `level` go black, at-or-above go white.

std:imageTranspose.label: Flip diagonal
std:imageTranspose.description: Swap rows and columns — main-diagonal reflection.

std:imageVignette.label: Vignette
std:imageVignette.description: Darken pixels radially from the center. `strength` 0..1 — 0 is no effect, 1 is full black at corners.

std:elem.label: Element of
std:elem.description: Test membership — `needle` is in `haystack` when haystack is a string containing the needle's JS string conversion as a substring (`contains`; as `toString needle` except that null and undefined convert to "null" and "undefined", never ""), or a list containing a structurally equal element (equivalent to `includes haystack needle` under stock equality: NaN never found, closures by identity); any other haystack is False. This fixed bootstrap leaf does not follow reader equality overrides. The compiled parser and resolver owners retain it as a host leaf over their verified string/finite-number domain.

std:eq.label: Equals
std:eq.description: Check equality (==). numeric-tower Phase 5 (D6): the declared type is the POLYMORPHIC Eq-method shape `t -> t -> Boolean`, NOT the anomalous String-only `(a:String)->(b:String)->Boolean` (it was always used generically; the JS impl is loose `==`). This native is the global total-Boolean FAST PATH; the principled API is the `Eq.eq : a -> a -> Maybe Bool` class method (per-rung instances in dispatch-instances.fenel). Behaviour unchanged — the String `Eq` IS the lexical compare (the LLVM `llvmHasStringTypedArg` String-escape keys on call-site arg types, not this decl, and stays); the DirectOp `F64Eq`/`oeq` lowering keys on the fnId, not this decl.

std:float32ToBytesLE.label: F32 → 4 bytes (little-endian)
std:float32ToBytesLE.description: Encode a Number as the 4-byte little-endian byte sequence of its IEEE 754 single-precision representation (each byte 0–255). Mirrors the `new Float32Array([n]) → new Uint8Array(buffer)` round-trip on a little-endian host. The primitive byte-iteration surface for binary serializers — e.g. Wasm's `f32.const` operand encoding.

std:float64ToBytesLE.label: F64 → 8 bytes (little-endian)
std:float64ToBytesLE.description: Encode an IEEE 754 double as its 8-byte little-endian byte sequence (each byte 0–255). Mirrors the `new Float64Array([n]) → new Uint8Array(buffer)` round-trip on a little-endian host. The primitive byte-iteration surface for binary serializers — e.g. Wasm's `f64.const` operand encoding.

std:merge.label: Merge
std:merge.description: Flatten and concatenate arrays — non-array values are wrapped as singletons. Variadic.

std:neq.label: Not equals
std:neq.description: Check inequality (!=). numeric-tower Phase 5 (D6): the declared type is the POLYMORPHIC Eq-method shape `t -> t -> Boolean`, NOT the anomalous String-only form. The global total-Boolean FAST PATH; the principled API is `Eq.neq : a -> a -> Maybe Bool` (per-rung instances). Behaviour unchanged (loose `!=`).

std:shiftLeft.label: Shift left
std:shiftLeft.description: Shift bits left by `n`. Int → Int → Int.

std:shiftRight.label: Shift right
std:shiftRight.description: Shift bits right by `n` (sign-extending). Int → Int → Int.

std:shiftRightU.label: Shift right (unsigned)
std:shiftRightU.description: Shift bits right by `n` (zero-fill, unsigned). Mirrors JS `>>>`. Distinct from `shiftRight` (which is sign-extending — JS `>>`). Required for LEB128 encoders walking u32 values past the 2^31 boundary, where sign-extension would yield the wrong continuation bits.

std:substr.label: Substring
std:substr.description: Extract substring from start (optionally for `len` codepoints). Negative `len` counts from the end.

std:truthy.label: Truthy
std:truthy.description: Coerce a value to its boolean truthiness. Mirrors JS truthiness semantics.

std:exp.label: Exponential
std:exp.description: e raised to the power x

std:mod.label: Modulo
std:mod.description: Remainder of a divided by b

std:camelCase.label: camelCase
std:camelCase.description: Convert to camelCase: lowercase first word, then capitalize each subsequent word.

std:canonical.label: Canonical string
std:canonical.description: Coerce a LocaleString (plain string or { locale: string, ... } record) to its canonical plain-string form. Used by Fenel-language renderers that need to stitch labels into a final user-facing message.

std:capitalize.label: Capitalize
std:capitalize.description: Uppercase the first character; leave the rest untouched.

std:chars.label: Chars
std:chars.description: Split into individual characters by Unicode code point. Emoji and non-BMP scripts stay grouped.

std:decodeUriComponent.label: URL-decode
std:decodeUriComponent.description: Percent-decode a URL component (decodeURIComponent semantics). Irreducible host substrate leaf — UTF-8 percent-decoding has no pure-Fenel form; the symmetric sister of std:urlEncode. Used by auth:parseCookieHeader to decode cookie values.

std:endsWith.label: Ends with
std:endsWith.description: Check if string ends with suffix

std:entries.label: Entries
std:entries.description: Convert a record into a list of {key, value} pairs. ∀a. Record String a → List {key: String, value: a}. Phase 13a-1: enables Fenel-side iteration over Record<String, _> shapes (handleList expansion in profiles, applyMapping in imports) — previously kept wrapper-side TS because std lacked entries/keys/values primitives.

std:fromEntries.label: From entries
std:fromEntries.description: The O(n) inverse of `entries`: build a record from a list of {key, value} pairs in ONE pass. ∀a. List {key: String, value: a} → Record String a. FIRST occurrence of a key wins (a later duplicate is dropped) — mirrors a first-match assoc-list lookup. parser-substrate 7h S2: the opaque-map perf branch — folding an index with the immutable-spread `mapSet` is O(n²), so this builds the lookup index O(n) for the parser's env (the pure assoc-list stays the source of truth; this is the JS-object index perf rep).

std:mapGet.label: Map get
std:mapGet.description: Read a record field by a DYNAMIC string key, returning Maybe (Just value when the key is present, Nothing when absent). ∀a. Record String a → String → Maybe a. The O(1) READ sibling of `mapSet` — genuinely inexpressible in a `.fenel` body because `.field` access is static-keyed. parser-substrate 7h S2: the opaque-map perf branch that makes the parser's env lookups (findEntry/lookupBool/lookupVal/bodyOf) constant-time over a `fromEntries`-built index; the pure assoc-list stays the source of truth.

std:evalExpr.label: Evaluate expression
std:evalExpr.description: Evaluate a stored JSON-Logic expression-value against a data record — the engine's own `evaluate` surfaced reflectively to a Fenel body (expression-as-runtime-value, design/expression-mobility-and-policy.md). NOT a new dialect: it IS the canonical evaluator, made Fenel-callable. Uses the default (EMPTY_CTX) evaluate — built-in ops + `var` reads only, no user-function dispatch — which is exact parity with the form-submit wrapper's `evaluate(expr, data)`. Pure (deterministic, no IO). The stored expr stays inert data until this call (the body reaches it only via a `var` read), so passing JSON-Logic through a body's params is safe without quoting. Added in Phase 5a-submit of the ts-elimination-completion workstream — the form-trigger / on-submit-rule condition evaluator the loops fold over.

std:format.label: Format template
std:format.description: Substitute `{name}` placeholders in a template string with values pulled from the args record. Missing keys leave the placeholder in place. Substitution is shallow — nested objects are coerced to a JSON-ish string.

std:join.label: Join
std:join.description: Join array of strings with separator

std:kebabCase.label: kebab-case
std:kebabCase.description: Convert to kebab-case: lowercase words separated by hyphens.

std:length.label: Length
std:length.description: Length of a list (or code-point count of a string, since String = List Char). ∀a. List a → ℕ

std:lines.label: Lines
std:lines.description: Split on newline boundaries (Unix or Windows).

std:mapDelete.label: Map delete
std:mapDelete.description: Return a new record with `key` removed. Missing key is a no-op. Original record is not mutated.

std:mapSet.label: Map set
std:mapSet.description: Return a new record with `key` bound to `value`. Existing key is replaced; missing key is added. Original record is not mutated.

std:padEnd.label: Pad end
std:padEnd.description: Pad string at end to target length

std:padStart.label: Pad start
std:padStart.description: Pad string at start to target length

std:parseInput.label: Parse input
std:parseInput.description: Run the type-driven input parser registered for the given FenelType (peels Maybe / $opaque / $refined, dispatches to the format-specific parser when one is registered, falls through to pass-through). Returns a result record `{ ok: Boolean, value?: a, error?: String }`.

std:parseJsonRows.label: Parse JSON rows
std:parseJsonRows.description: Parse a JSON-text string into a List of records: `JSON.parse(s)`, then array-coerce (a top-level array passes through; a single object is wrapped to a one-element list). Irreducible host-marshalling leaf — arbitrary-JSON-text parsing has no reasonable pure-Fenel form (same bridge class as the host-string leaves urlEncode / regexSet). Pure (deterministic, no IO). Throws on malformed JSON (parity with the wrapper-side `JSON.parse` it replaces). Added in Phase 5a-csv of the ts-elimination-completion workstream — the JSON fork of imports:parseRows.

std:replace.label: Replace
std:replace.description: Replace first occurrence of pattern with replacement

std:replaceAll.label: Replace all
std:replaceAll.description: Replace every occurrence of `find` with `replacement`. Unlike `replace` (single occurrence), this swaps all of them.

std:slice.label: Slice
std:slice.description: Extract substring from start to end index

std:slugify.label: Slugify
std:slugify.description: URL-safe slug: lowercase ASCII letters/digits, collapse runs of other chars to single hyphens, trim leading/trailing hyphens.

std:snakeCase.label: snake_case
std:snakeCase.description: Convert to snake_case: lowercase words separated by underscores.

std:startsWith.label: Starts with
std:startsWith.description: Check if string starts with prefix

std:titleCase.label: Title case
std:titleCase.description: Uppercase the first letter of each word, lowercase the rest.

std:tryParseInt.label: Try parse Int
std:tryParseInt.description: Attempt to parse a string as an Int. Trims whitespace; rejects empty / non-finite / fractional inputs. Returns Just<n> on success, Nothing otherwise. Added in Phase 11c sub-step 3 of the ts-elimination workstream — substrate primitive used by stepConversation's `collector:N` callback index parsing.

std:urlEncode.label: URL-encode
std:urlEncode.description: Percent-encode a string for safe inclusion in a URL component (encodeURIComponent semantics). Irreducible host substrate leaf — UTF-8 percent-encoding has no pure-Fenel form. Used by telegram:deepLink for the `?start=<payload>` query value.

std:validateValue.label: Validate value
std:validateValue.description: Validate a value against any FenelType using the universal engine validator (refinements, enums, intervals, $tagged entity refs, …). Returns `{ ok: Boolean, error?: String }` where `error` joins all failing constraints. Pure — no IO. Pairs with parseInput: parse first to get a typed value, then validate the value against its declared field type.

std:words.label: Words
std:words.description: Split into words on any run of whitespace. Empty input → empty list.

std:charFromCode.label: Char from code point
std:charFromCode.description: Single-character string from a Unicode code point (or UTF-16 code unit, for code points < 0x10000). Mirrors JS `String.fromCodePoint`. The inverse of indexing into `chars s`; useful for serializers walking byte sequences (e.g. LLVM IR's printable-ASCII passthrough in string-constant emission).

std:charCode.label: Char to code point
std:charCode.description: Unicode code point of a single character (the first code point if given a longer string; 0 for the empty string). Mirrors JS `.codePointAt(0)`. The irreducible host leaf that maps a Char's runtime repr (a one-character String — `Char = $opaque { repr: "codepoint", pure: Nat ∈ unicode-scalars }`, surfaced as a 1-char string at the boundary) to its ordinal. The inverse of `charFromCode`; the substrate that lets pure-Fenel `charLt` / `strCompare` (ord.fenel) order Char/String lexically. set-algebra-to-fenel Phase 3b-3 (string-ordering enabler).

std:isArray.label: Is array
std:isArray.description: Check if value is a JS array. Phase 5b14 added this to support the bare-array-at-expression-position lowering in `engine:normaliseToCore` — the per-target CeLit lowerings (`lower-to-wasm-ast.fenel`'s `lowerWasmLit`, `lower-to-llvm-ast.fenel`'s `lowerLlvmLit`) gain an isArray arm that emits the empty-list base case as a target-appropriate null reference (the WASM / LLVM runtime helpers treat null as empty list end-to-end).

std:isBytes.label: Is bytes
std:isBytes.description: Recognize the Uint8Array host carrier of Bytes by its intrinsic brand and readable storage, without coercion or reading candidate properties. Detached views, other typed arrays, proxies and prototype imitations are not byte values.

std:isBoolean.label: Is boolean
std:isBoolean.description: Check if value is a boolean

std:isNull.label: Is null
std:isNull.description: Check if value is null or undefined

std:isNumber.label: Is number
std:isNumber.description: Check if value is a number

std:isString.label: Is string
std:isString.description: Check if value is a string

std:jsLit.label: JS literal encode
std:jsLit.description: Encode a value as a JS-source-valid string literal. Wraps `JSON.stringify` — produces `"hi"` for the string `hi`, `42` for the number `42`, `true` / `false` for booleans, `null` for null. The encode-side primitive used by `serializeJsModule`'s JsLit and JsObject-key arms to emit JS-source-valid output that round-trips through `eval` / dynamic-import.

std:numberIsFinite.label: Number is finite
std:numberIsFinite.description: True iff the number is neither NaN nor positive/negative Infinity. Mirrors JS `Number.isFinite`. Useful for serializers that need to special-case the non-finite IEEE 754 values (e.g. LLVM IR's hex-bit-pattern form for NaN/Inf doubles).

std:numberToHex.label: Number to hex
std:numberToHex.description: Render a non-negative integer in uppercase hexadecimal, zero-padded to `minDigits`. Mirrors JS `n.toString(16).toUpperCase().padStart(minDigits, "0")`. Phase 11b sub-step 3 substrate addition — used by `runtime:quotedPrintable` for the `=XX` RFC 2045 encoding of non-printable bytes. Negative or non-integer inputs follow JS's `toString(16)` semantics (the caller is responsible for clamping to byte range when used as a byte-encoder).

std:utf8Bytes.label: UTF-8 bytes
std:utf8Bytes.description: Encode a string as its UTF-8 byte sequence (each byte as a Number 0–255). The primitive byte-iteration surface for serializers — e.g. LLVM IR's `[N x i8] c"…"` string constants, JSON byte-pretty-printers. `length (utf8Bytes s)` is the byte length (NOT the code-point count returned by `length s`).

std:typeOf.label: Type of
std:typeOf.description: Return the FenelType of a value as a first-class Type. Conflate-free: the type's display name is `codeName (typeOf v)` via the Codeable typeclass, not a property of the value itself.

std:vecOfLength.label: Vec of length
std:vecOfLength.description: Type-level: return the FenelType `Vec(elemType, n)` — a list of `elemType` of exactly `n` elements. Use under `$el { call: ["vecOfLength", T, { var: "n" }] }` when `n` comes from a sibling field.

std:lengthBoundedStringOf.label: Length-bounded String
std:lengthBoundedStringOf.description: Type-level: return the FenelType `LengthBoundedString(n)` — a String of exactly `n` codepoints. Use under `$el { call: ["lengthBoundedStringOf", { var: "n" }] }` when `n` comes from a sibling field.

std:exactValueEqual.label: Exact value equality
std:exactValueEqual.description: Decide whether two values are the same value with the engine's exact value equality (the owner that decides enum membership): Just true or Just false when it decides, Nothing when it cannot (unreadable, host-shaped or oversized data, an undecided numeric owner). Records and variants compare field by field; callables compare by identity; $ref handles compare as their handle text; NaN is never equal. ∀a. a → a → Maybe Bool

std:groupFold.label: Group fold
std:groupFold.description: Shared left-to-right grouping traversal for groupBy and groupByKey: computes each element's key exactly once, in list order, and asks the insert step to place the element; stops at the first step that cannot decide (Nothing) without computing later keys. Internal helper.

std:groupByRecordInsert.label: Group by (record insert)
std:groupByRecordInsert.description: Legacy text-keyed insert step for groupBy: append the element to the record field named by its key (the record coerces the key to text), keeping first-encounter key order. Always decides. Internal helper.

std:groupByKeyInsert.label: Group by key (insert)
std:groupByKeyInsert.description: Place one element into the typed groups: append it to the first group whose key is exactly equal, else add a new group at the end. Nothing when a key comparison cannot be decided. Internal helper for groupByKey.

std:groupByKey.label: Group by key
std:groupByKey.description: Group elements by a key function, keeping each actual key value (a record, a date, any type) with its members. Keys are compared with the engine's exact value equality: records and variants field by field, callables by identity, $ref handles by their handle text, NaN never equal. Groups and members keep encounter order and each group keeps its first key. Nothing when a key comparison is undecided. ∀a k. (a → k) → List a → Maybe (Map k (List a))

std:mapValues.label: Map values
std:mapValues.description: Apply a function to every value of a Map, keeping each key and the entry order. ∀k v w. (v → w) → Map k v → Map k w

std:countByKey.label: Count by key
std:countByKey.description: Count the elements of each group of groupByKey: one entry per key (first-encounter order) with its number of elements. Nothing when a key comparison is undecided. ∀a k. (a → k) → List a → Maybe (Map k Number)

std:sumByKey.label: Sum by key
std:sumByKey.description: Sum a number of each element per group of groupByKey: one entry per key (first-encounter order) with the sum of its elements' amounts. Nothing when a key comparison is undecided. ∀a k. (a → k) → (a → Number) → List a → Maybe (Map k Number)

std:sortAscending.label: Sort ascending
std:sortAscending.description: The items in ascending order: `sort` keyed by each item itself, stably. Items std lt cannot compare are a tie and keep encounter order. ∀a. List a → List a

std:intersection.label: Intersection
std:intersection.description: Keep each element of the first list that occurs in the second under ordinary structural eq. Preserve the first list's order and duplicates.

std:subsequences.label: Subsequences
std:subsequences.description: Every order-preserving selection from the list, including the empty selection. Repeated input positions remain separate choices; n items produce 2^n selections.

std:imageFromPackedRgba.label: Image from packed RGBA
std:imageFromPackedRgba.description: Decode decimal RGBA words into ordinary row-major Image data. A wrong word count produces the empty image.

std:imageFromPalette.label: Image from a palette
std:imageFromPalette.description: Decode a palette picture into ordinary row-major Image data: the palette is at most 64 decimal RGBA words separated by spaces (as imageFromPackedRgba reads them), the letters are one character per pixel, row-major, from the alphabet 0-9, A-Z, a-z, + and /, where the i-th letter names the i-th palette word. A letter outside the palette, more than 64 words, or a letter count other than width times height produces the empty image.

std:imageSourceOverPixel.label: Source-over RGBA pixel
std:imageSourceOverPixel.description: Composite straight RGBA raster coverage using both alpha channels; round/clamp byte channels after unassociation. Fully transparent results are transparent black. Shared by imageOverlay and picture.alphaBlend.

std:bytesToList.label: Bytes as a list
std:bytesToList.description: Copy the readable Uint8Array representation of Bytes into its ordinary List Byte view. This host representation bridge does not call candidate iterators or read candidate properties. Text decoding and validation belong to Fenel bodies.

std:colorFromHertz.label: Color from hertz
std:colorFromHertz.description: Admit a finite positive hertz value as Color. Zero, negative, nonnumeric and nonfinite inputs return Err. No wavelength or frequency is inferred from RGB.

std:humanSpectrumColorType.label: Type of human-spectrum Color
std:humanSpectrumColorType.description: Narrow Color to an authored observer band's closed interval using the existing refinement and SetExpr machinery. Invalid bounds produce the empty type. The chosen band is model data, not a universal visibility claim.

std:humanSpectrumColor.label: Color in an observer band
std:humanSpectrumColor.description: The frequency parameter's type depends on the selected observer band. The same source checks the supplied frequency and refuses invalid or outside-band data; it reads no clock or host observation.

std:normalizeSpectrum.label: Normalize a finite spectrum
std:normalizeSpectrum.description: Validate at most 128 input components, merge exactly equal Number frequencies, omit zero weights and retain at most 64 distinct frequencies. Invalid data or weight overflow returns Err. Order follows the first contributing occurrence; no frequency is averaged.

std:addSpectra.label: Add spectra
std:addSpectra.description: Add independent spectral contributions. Equal frequencies sum their weights; distinct frequencies remain separate. Each input has at most 64 components; overflow or more than 64 resulting distinct frequencies refuses.

std:blendSpectra.label: Blend spectra with explicit opacity
std:blendSpectra.description: Compute opacity times foreground plus (1-opacity) times background. Opacity is an explicit finite coefficient from 0 through 1, never a field of Color or Spectrum. This is a mixture of contributions; frequencies are not interpolated.

std:rgbToSpectrum.label: RGB coordinates to spectrum
std:rgbToSpectrum.description: Weight the three distinct positive frequencies in an explicitly supplied primary profile. Red/green/blue are finite linear coefficients from 0 through 1. White retains three contributions; purple retains red and blue. No measured sRGB spectra or single-frequency inverse is invented.

std:hslToSpectrum.label: HSL coordinates to spectrum
std:hslToSpectrum.description: Convert finite hue degrees from 0 through 360 and saturation/lightness from 0 through 1 into RGB coefficients of the supplied primary profile, then retain their weighted Spectrum. Hue 360 equals 0. This is the declared coordinate model, not a calibrated perceptual or measured sRGB spectrum.

std:spectrumToRgb.label: Spectrum to declared RGB coordinates
std:spectrumToRgb.description: A partial projection into the supplied profile's three-frequency basis. Other frequencies refuse; accumulated coefficients above 1 refuse rather than clipping. The original Spectrum remains the source. This is not a physical spectrum reconstruction or a reversible Reprable instance.

std:filterSpectrum.label: Apply an explicit spectral filter
std:filterSpectrum.description: Multiply each frequency's weight by an explicitly supplied finite transmission from 0 through 1. Require at most 64 spectrum/filter entries and one filter entry per frequency; missing contributing frequencies refuse. This declares a transmission model, not a physical pigment model or frequency subtraction.

std:documentReadPlan.label: Preview document
std:documentReadPlan.description: Derive safe markup and ordinary typed embedded data from the same document tree. Heading depth follows section nesting, capped at HTML heading level six.

std:documentPlainText.label: Document as plain text
std:documentPlainText.description: Extract headings, link labels, code, notes, embedded scalar/list data and captions from the same document. Styling is removed, nonempty blocks are separated by blank lines, and text/code contents remain literal.

std:documentOutline.label: Document outline
std:documentOutline.description: List section headings in document order with their actual nesting depth. Titles use the same plain-text projection; notes preserve the surrounding section depth.

std:documentToMarkdown.label: Document as Markdown
std:documentToMarkdown.description: Export sections/paragraphs, composed emphasis/strong, code, safe links and notes as CommonMark with XHTML for inline styling/links, notes and exact block-code fallbacks. Text punctuation/whitespace stays literal; code delimiters avoid source collisions. Embeds, invalid characters, unsafe links, multiline headings/inline code and excessive nesting return Err. documentFromMarkdown reads a declared bounded fragment with outline/text normalization: normalized-value round trips apply to representable outline-shaped trees within its source bound, not arbitrary authored section endings.

std:documentToHtml.label: Document as HTML
std:documentToHtml.description: Export sections/paragraphs, composed emphasis/strong, code, safe links and notes as a deterministic XHTML-compatible HTML fragment. Escape text/attributes with the shared HTML primitive and encode TAB/LF/CR as numeric references. The character fragment excludes invalid XML scalars, other C0/C1 controls and Unicode noncharacters. Embeds, unsafe links, multiline headings and excessive nesting return Err. documentFromHtml reads this fragment within its source-size bound, normalizing only text-node boundaries.

std:documentFromHtml.label: Document from HTML
std:documentFromHtml.description: Import the bounded lowercase XHTML-style fragment emitted by Document as HTML into the same typed Document.
